headline: Record revenue, but record fuel costs cut profit
summary_short: Delta posted record June-quarter revenue of $19.8B (+18.7% y/y) and rebounded from a Q1 net loss to $1,604M in net income, but the highest quarterly fuel expense in company history cut operating margin to 9.4% from 12.6% a year ago (-11.3%).
summary_long: Revenue rose 18.7% y/y to a record $19.8B on broad demand strength, ~1% capacity growth, and diversified revenue (61% of total, +2pts y/y) including premium +17%, cargo +39%, and loyalty +19%. Operating income fell 11.3% y/y to $1,864M as adjusted fuel price rose 75% y/y to $3.93/gal — the highest quarterly fuel expense in company history — pushing operating margin down 320bps to 9.4%. Net income of $1,604M (-24.7% y/y) rebounded sharply from Q1's $289M loss. Cash was $4,665M and long-term debt eased to $12,905M (-10.3% y/y). Delta reaffirmed FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $6.50-$7.50 and guided September-quarter EPS to $2.00-$2.50.
